subject: English Language
name: Basic 2 English Language
description: The Basic 2 English Language curriculum builds on Basic 1, focusing on deeper engagement with listening, speaking, reading, and writing. It emphasizes culturally acceptable language, reading fluency, comprehension strategies, and writing conventions within an integrated, thematic framework.

strands.title: Oral Language (Listening and Speaking)
strands.description: Enhancing listening and speaking skills through songs, rhymes, storytelling, dramatisation, conversation, and presentation.

subStrands.title: Songs
subStrands.description: Demonstrating understanding of a variety of songs.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of a variety of songs

indicators.description: Interpret familiar songs

exemplars.description: Identify some familiar songs from learners' locality.
Teach the songs with themes from their locality.
Discuss the moral values of the songs.
Let learners sing songs using gestures appropriately.
Have learners interpret the songs in their own words.

subStrands.title: Rhymes
subStrands.description: Showing understanding of literary pieces.

contentStandards.description: Show understanding of a variety of literary pieces.

indicators.description: Interpret rhymes and tongue-twisters in own words

exemplars.description: Revise some familiar rhymes and tongue-twisters learnt.
Select a rhyme from learners.
As learners listen and observe, perform the rhyme (Recite it, accompanied with actions and gestures, two or three times).
Recite lines of the rhyme as learners join in and repeat lines after you.
Teach the accompanying actions through demonstration.
Let learners repeat lines of the rhyme on their own accompanied with appropriate actions.
Through questions, have learners interpret the rhymes in their own words.

subStrands.title: Story Telling
subStrands.description: Responding to stories.

contentStandards.description: Respond to stories

indicators.description: Identify characters in a story and relate them to real life situations

exemplars.description: Choose a story from learners' background.
Tell the story with appropriate actions, gestures, facial expressions, etc.
Have learners retell the story and answer questions on it.
Let learners say whether or not they have enjoyed the story and why.
Put learners into groups to identify the characters and their actions and relate them to real life situations. NOTE. Use pictures/sketches, real objects, etc.

indicators.description: Retell stories sequentially, following story structure (beginning, middle and ending)

exemplars.description: Revise the previous story told by having learners recall some of the characters.
Discuss the moral lessons/values of the story.
Let learners retell the story sequentially, following story structure (beginning, middle and ending).
Let learners relate the story to real life situations.

indicators.description: Tell stories from cultural background

exemplars.description: Revise some stories learners have heard.
Tell the story as learners listen.
Let learners tell their own stories.
Discuss the moral lessons/values in stories told.

subStrands.title: Dramatisation and Role Play
subStrands.description: Performing stories.

contentStandards.description: Perform Stories

indicators.description: Dramatise/role-play stories heard or read

exemplars.description: Have learners select an interesting story heard or read in class.
Retell the story.
Discuss the story and have learners recall main events and characters.
Select characters and assign them roles to play.
Let learners dramatise/role-play the story.
Discuss moral values from the story.
Have learners say whether or not they have enjoyed the drama and why.

subStrands.title: Conversation
subStrands.description: Talking about Oneself, Family, People, Places, Customs, Events, Social/Cultural Values, Manners and other Themes.

contentStandards.description: Use certain culturally acceptable language for communication

indicators.description: Use appropriate greetings for special occasions

exemplars.description: Revise daily greetings by having learners identify greeting times in the day: e.g. Morning-Good morning, Afternoon-Good afternoon, Evening-Good evening.
Discuss special occasions such as birthdays, anniversaries and festivals.
Discuss the correct greetings and responses on these occasions.
Let learners take turns to demonstrate greetings for special occasions and also practise the appropriate responses.

indicators.description: Talk about events at home

exemplars.description: Introduce the day's topic and show pictures of activities at home.
Have learners think-pair-share the domestic activities.
Have learners talk about which of the events they like most and why they like them.
Have learners role-play some of the scenes. E.g. People engaged in domestic chores. People at table.

indicators.description: Talk about things and places in their homes

exemplars.description: Ask learners to name things and places in their homes and say what happens at those places.

Show pictures of important places in their community, such as the chief's palace, the market, the police station, etc. and have learners think-pair-share ideas or views with the person sitting next to them.
Put learners into groups to talk about their pictures.
Rotate the pictures until each group has had its turn to talk about all the pictures.

indicators.description: Use a wide variety of words to talk about manners

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of language and communicative skills to participate in conversation

indicators.description: Demonstrate turn-taking in conversations

exemplars.description: Use the Community Circle Activity: Sit learners in horse-shoe formation.
Call individual learners to talk about what happened over the weekend. e. g. events, personal experiences, incidents, etc.
Let learners take turns to name and describe events of recent occurrence.
Discuss the importance of turn-taking in conversation: e.g. i. They talk after the last speaker has stopped. ii. They talk when invited e.g. by the group leader.

indicators.description: Ask and answer questions for clarifications about what other people say

exemplars.description: Have learners recall the discussion on turn-taking in conversation and state the rules.
Encourage learners to ask and answer questions for clarification on what other learners have said.
Encourage appropriate language use during conversations.

subStrands.title: Listening Comprehension
subStrands.description: Using appropriate skills and strategies to process meaning from texts.

contentStandards.description: Use appropriate skills and strategies to process meaning from texts

indicators.description: Listen to and interact actively with drama

exemplars.description: Before Reading: Activate the previous knowledge of the learners by making them think pair and share with their friends. Discuss illustrations accompanying the text. Have them predict the content of the text. Teach key vocabulary.
During Reading: Read the text aloud to learners. Pause often and have learners talk about the content of the text and answer simple questions based on the text.
After Reading: Have learners retell the story. Let learners role-play the story.

indicators.description: Recognise and relate the sequence of events (beginning, middle and end) in drama

exemplars.description: Read a narrative text aloud to learners, following the procedure in B2.1.6.1.2.
Put learners in groups to identify and talk about the parts of the drama (beginning, middle and ending).

indicators.description: Recognise and discuss events in a story (characters, settings, moral, etc.)

exemplars.description: Read aloud a story to learners.
Have them identify and discuss (in pairs) the events in the story.
Have groups share their views with the whole class.

indicators.description: Share facts from texts heard with a partner, groups or the teacher

exemplars.description: Read an information text aloud to learners, using the KWL Strategy.

KWL Strategy: Before reading, have learners think-pair-share and talk about what they already know(K) about the title of the text. Have learners ask questions about what they want to know (W). While you read the text, pause often to give the children the chance to share what they have learned or answer the questions they have asked before reading.
After the reading, have learners share what they have learned. Put learners in groups to share facts from the text heard.

subStrands.title: Asking and Answering Questions
subStrands.description: Demonstrating understanding in asking and answering questions.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding in asking and answering questions

indicators.description: Use appropriate pronunciation and intonation in asking and answering Wh - questions

exemplars.description: Revise Yes/No questions and have learners answer some such question
Ask Wh questions and have learners answer them. e.g. Questions: Who took my pen? Where is the book? Answers: I did. It is on the table.
Ask them to say what is common to all the questions introduced by Wh words (what? when? why? how?). e.g. Why did you eat her food?
Guide learners to use appropriate pronunciation and intonation in asking and answering simple Wh-questions in pairs. One asks a Wh question and the other answers. They then reverse roles.
Let learners write out simple Wh - questions on their own.

subStrands.title: Giving and Responding to Commands, Instructions, Directions and Making Requests
subStrands.description: Demonstrating understanding in commands, instructions, directions and requests.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding in commands, instructions, directions and requests

indicators.description: Give and respond to commands

exemplars.description: Revise verbs (action words) by having learners identify the present form of verbs and use them in sentences, e.g. come, go, sit, etc. (action).
Have several learners obey commands such as 'stand up', 'close the door'.
The teacher gives commands which the class/individuals promptly obey.
Have Learners role-play giving and responding to commands.

indicators.description: Make and respond to polite requests

exemplars.description: Let learners demonstrate in pairs how they ask for favours.
Discuss polite requests using examples. e. g. Can you hold the bag?
Discuss words used in polite requests. e.g. Please, could you..., do you mind.... May I...
Have learners take turns to make and respond to polite requests using the word, "please".
Discuss the importance of the word, "please", in making requests.

indicators.description: Respond to commands, instructions and requests

exemplars.description: Introduce instructions by having learners respond to typical classroom instructions.
Create situations for learners to practise giving and responding to instruction.
Let learners role-play parents, teachers, prefects, learners giving and responding to instructions, etc. e. g. Instruction: 1. Draw a circle in a square. 2. Write the letter 'A' in the circle.

subStrands.title: Presentation
subStrands.description: Planning and presenting information and ideas for a variety of purposes.

contentStandards.description: Plan and present information and ideas for a variety of purposes

indicators.description: Speak with confidence before different audience

exemplars.description: Put learners in pairs to share their holiday plans with each other.
Have each person share his/her friend's plans with the class.
Use probing questions to get learners give additional information: e.g. i. Where will he go first? ii. What will he be doing there? etc.

indicators.description: Maintain appropriate posture, eye contact and use appropriate verbal and non-verbal cues to convey meaning

exemplars.description: Model appropriate posture, eye contact and use verbal and non-verbal clues.
Let learners observe and do same.
Discuss when to use various postures, eye contact, verbal and non-verbal clues when talking to different people e.g. teacher, friend.
Have learners role-play how to maintain appropriate posture, verbal and non-verbal clues in communication. e.g. crossed arms and unblinking eye gaze to indicate disapproval.

strands.title: Reading
strands.description: Developing reading skills through phonics, word families, vocabulary, comprehension, and fluency.

subStrands.title: Phonics
subStrands.description: Connecting sounds to letters and blending them to read and write.

contentStandards.description: Connect sounds to letters and blend letters/syllables in order to read and write

indicators.description: Blend syllables to produce words

exemplars.description: Introduce the lesson with a recital that links the letters of the alphabet.
Have learners work in pairs, groups or individually to blend syllables to form meaningful words.
Use word families as a guide to help build on the words.

indicators.description: Use the alphabetic knowledge to decode unknown words (e. g. use beginning and ending consonants, consonant blends, consonant digraphs, vowel sounds, vowel digraphs and word patterns)

exemplars.description: Begin the lesson with an alphabet song, a rhyme or a poem.
Play games with the alphabet to decode unknown words, changing the position of the letters from beginning to middle and to ending.
Use demonstrations to show learners that whenever a letter moves (especially the consonant), it may still sound the same.
Have learners play alphabet games in pairs and groups.

indicators.description: Use elements of structural analysis to decode unknown words.

exemplars.description: Have learners analyse the basic structure of unknown two-syllable words using specific indicators as a guide (root words, prefixes like un-, suffixes like -ly).
Let learners look at the different features of compound words.
Give learners the opportunity to work as teams/groups to come up with their own features, e. g. "class" and "room" will give "classroom".

subStrands.title: Word Families-Rhyming Endings and Common Digraphs
subStrands.description: Using rhyming endings and digraphs to enhance reading comprehension.

contentStandards.description: Employ knowledge of rhyming endings and common digraphs to enhance reading comprehension

indicators.description: Use common rhyming/endings to decode simple words

exemplars.description: Introduce learners to simple word formation by changing the beginning letter of words. e.g. pan, man, fan (You may use a phonic slide to give practice).
Have learners build on these rhyming endings.
In groups, let learners read out their words.
Have learners form sentences with these rhyming words.

indicators.description: Use words containing digraphs to make meaningful sentences.

exemplars.description: Introduce learners to simple digraphs as in; ch- church, ph- photo, sh - shirt.
Have learners build as many words as possible from digraphs.
Have learners form meaningful sentences with the words.

subStrands.title: Vocabulary
subStrands.description: Understanding word meanings and usages.

contentStandards.description: Understand word meanings and usages

indicators.description: Read level-appropriate sight words, understand and use many of them in meaningful sentences

exemplars.description: Introduce the selected sight words, one at a time, in context and write them on the board.
Start from the basic words they already know.
Have learners repeat the words aloud a number of times.
Write the words on the board.
Have learners read the words in order and at random.
Use think-pair-share to have learners form sentences with them.

indicators.description: Use context clues to infer meanings of words

exemplars.description: Create a story around a theme, using specific key words or vocabulary items you wish to teach.
Have learners use context to find the meaning of the key words.
Have learners make their own sentences using these key words.

indicators.description: Show awareness that homonyms have different meanings in different contexts

exemplars.description: Provide examples in contexts to help learners discover that homonyms have different meanings in different contexts. e.g. right and bat. a. You are right. Raise your right hand. b. I saw a bat fly this morning. My mother bought a tennis bat for me.

indicators.description: Use dictionaries and glossaries to clarify meaning of words

exemplars.description: Introduce learners to the use of picture dictionaries and glossaries.
Have learners use guide words to find meaning of words used.
Have learners practise in pairs.

subStrands.title: Comprehension
subStrands.description: Understanding and analysing texts read.

contentStandards.description: Understand and analyse texts read

indicators.description: Use illustrations, text clues and context to make predictions during reading

exemplars.description: Have learners use text features like title, illustrations and text clues to make meaning and inferences.
Have learners predict, brainstorm on the topic and have them read to confirm their predictions.
Have learners pause frequently during reading to make predictions to enhance comprehension.

indicators.description: Ask and answer factual and inferential questions about level-appropriate texts

exemplars.description: Have learners read level-appropriate texts in pairs.
Guide learners to ask and answer simple inferential questions on the texts.

indicators.description: Retell level-appropriate texts in own words

exemplars.description: Revise some previous stories told.
Have learners retell a story using simple herring-bone strategies.

contentStandards.description: Use knowledge skills and techniques of reading to understand and interpret texts

indicators.description: Demonstrate understanding of the purpose and features of information texts

exemplars.description: Have learners read informational texts to identify their purpose and features through think-pair-share.

indicators.description: Describe events in a story

exemplars.description: Have learners retell stories sequentially.
Have them identify and describe events in the stories.
Guide learners to unfold the events in a story sequentially.

indicators.description: Connect characters, ideas and information within a text

exemplars.description: Have learners connect the ideas and information within a text to help construct meaning.

indicators.description: Read level-appropriate texts with little support

exemplars.description: Have learners read different texts with little support from teacher.
Gradually, scaffold to help learners read independently.

indicators.description: Use visualisation strategy (form mental images about texts) to enhance understanding of level-appropriate texts

exemplars.description: Model using visualisation strategy to construct meaning from a text.
Through appropriate questions, guide learners to practise using visualisation strategy to construct meaning from texts. Note: visualisation strategy = forming mental image about texts.

subStrands.title: Fluency
subStrands.description: Reading texts with good speed, accuracy, and expression.

contentStandards.description: Read texts fluently

indicators.description: Read texts/stories/passages with good pace, accuracy and expression

exemplars.description: Model reading aloud with the focus on pace and expression.
Have learners, in group/pairs, read short texts aloud with the appropriate pace, accuracy and expression.

indicators.description: Read and recognise 120 sight words

exemplars.description: Introduce learners to more sight words in context.
Have them identify and use at least 120 sight-words.
Remember to focus on a few at a time.

indicators.description: Use contextual clues to confirm or self-correct pronunciation while reading aloud

exemplars.description: Have learners use the context in which words are found to confirm or self-correct pronunciation of words while they read aloud.
Check intonation as they read to make meaning.

strands.title: Using Writing Conventions/Grammar Usage
strands.description: Applying grammar rules and conventions in writing and communication.

subStrands.title: Using Capitalisation
subStrands.description: Using capital letters correctly in writing.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of capitalisation in writing

indicators.description: Use capital letter to write names of particular places and days of the week

exemplars.description: Provide a sample text and have learners identify names of particular places and days of the week.
Have them compare the initial letters of these names and other common names and share their observations with the class.

Give learners a text with names of particular places and days of the week, beginning with small letters. Let learners rewrite the text, beginning the names of particular places and days of the week, with capital letters.

indicators.description: Use capital letters to begin the first words of sentences

exemplars.description: Assist learners to begin sentences with capital letters. For example: i. Kofi is a good boy. ii. The house is beautiful.

subStrands.title: Using Punctuation
subStrands.description: Applying punctuation marks in writing.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of punctuation in written communication

indicators.description: Use full stops at the end of sentences and question marks at the end of questions

exemplars.description: Have learners look at sentences in their class readers to observe how they begin and end.
Demonstrate placing a full stop (.) at the end of a sentence.
Let learners copy and punctuate sentences with full stop.
Present the question mark similarly.

subStrands.title: Using Action Words
subStrands.description: Using verbs to express actions and states.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of action words in communication

indicators.description: Use the simple present tense to express habitual actions (simple truths, interest, feelings and opinions)

exemplars.description: Tell learners some of the things you do daily in short and simple sentences. e.g. I read stories everyday.
Create situations for learners to use the structure. e.g. i. simple truths - Lemons are sour. ii. interest - I like playing football. iii. feelings - I am happy. iv. opinions - He is a good teacher.
Introduce drills for learners to have practice.
Put learners into small groups to discuss given topics, using the structures.

subStrands.title: Using Adjectives
subStrands.description: Using adjectives to describe people and things.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of adjectives in communication

indicators.description: Identify and use simple sentences to describe the weather and show quantity and position or order of people and things

exemplars.description: Use appropriate texts to help learners to describe the weather and show quantity and position or order of people and things, e.g: weather - It is cold. quantity - I have two pens. position or order of people and things - She is on the first row.

subStrands.title: Using Simple Preposition
subStrands.description: Using prepositions to indicate time and place.

contentStandards.description: Understand and identify the use of prepositions

indicators.description: Identify prepositions in sentences to indicate days, dates and places

exemplars.description: Let learners use the preposition in, on, in context. e.g. i. I saw a bird on Monday. ii. I have a test on 1st May, 2018. iii. They are in the classroom.

indicators.description: Use prepositions to form simple sentences to indicate position and time

exemplars.description: Provide a short passage containing prepositions that indicate position and time.
Let learners identify the prepositions. e. g. i. Esi sat on a chair in the room. ii. The other pupils stood on the veranda. iii. The teacher went to the classroom at night.

subStrands.title: Using Simple and Compound Sentences
subStrands.description: Understanding sentence structure.

contentStandards.description: Understand simple sentences in writing

indicators.description: Identify the structure of simple sentences

exemplars.description: Use context to help learners identify the structure of simple sentences. Yaa came. (Name) + (Doing word) Musa ate.

indicators.description: Identify nouns and verbs in simple sentences

exemplars.description: Use questions and samples to learners to identify nouns and verbs in the structure of simple sentences. e. g. i. Ofori danced. (Who danced? What did Ofori do?) ii. Ama laughed.

subStrands.title: Spelling
subStrands.description: Using phonics to spell words.

contentStandards.description: Use phonics knowledge to spell words

indicators.description: Use phonics knowledge to spell words with irregular phonic letter pattern

exemplars.description: Have learners play the pick and spell game to spell phonetically irregular words. e. g. the, face
Have learners use these words in oral and written sentences.
Provide sentences with blank spaces for learners to fill in the blanks using the words they have learnt to spell. e. g. i. This is my-------

subStrands.title: Building The Love And Culture Of Reading
subStrands.description: Encouraging independent reading.

contentStandards.description: Read widely for pleasure and to demonstrate independent reading and learning in the literary area

indicators.description: Read a variety of age and level-appropriate books and texts from print and non-print

exemplars.description: Use the Author's chair to introduce the reading/ library time.
Have a variety of age and level-appropriate books for learners to make a choice.
Introduce narratives, pop-up and flip-the-page texts to learners.
Introduce e-books to learners, if available.
For each reading session, guide learners to select books.

strands.title: Writing
strands.description: Developing writing skills through penmanship, labelling, sentence construction, and composition.

subStrands.title: Penmanship/Handwriting
subStrands.description: Copying and rewriting sentences correctly.

contentStandards.description: Copy and rewrite sentences correctly

indicators.description: Copy sentences clearly

exemplars.description: Demonstrate copying (sentences) on the board.
Let learners practise writing legibly and correctly on the board or into their books.
Have learners copy sentences from a book into their books.
Draw attention to inter and intra word spacing and alignment of letters, as well as clarity or writing.

subStrands.title: Writing Letters - Small and Capital
subStrands.description: Using skills to write legibly and boldly.

contentStandards.description: Use general skills, strategies and knowledge of letter sounds to enable them write legibly and boldly

indicators.description: Copy words in lower and upper case using correct spacing

exemplars.description: Let learners write letters, both in upper and lower cases.
Copy words from learners' reading book on the board as learners observe.
Let learners take turns to read out words from the list.
Draw attention to appropriate spelling and alignment of letters.
Let learners copy the words. Let them check correct spelling, formation of letters and spacing.

indicators.description: Use lower and upper case letters appropriately in words and simple sentences

exemplars.description: Guide learners to choose level-appropriate topics. e. g. My Family, My Pet, My Friend, etc.
Let learners talk about the topic.
Write what learners say about the topic on the board. e. g. My family: There are six people in my family. My father is a teacher. My mother is a nurse, etc.
Have learners read the sentences.
Re-write the sentences with wrong capitalisation and ask learners re-write them appropriately. e. g. my Father is a teacher.

indicators.description: Space words appropriately in sentences

exemplars.description: Write the sentences on the board.
Let learners copy the sentences, paying attention to spacing of words in the sentence.
Encourage learners to display their work.

subStrands.title: Labelling Items
subStrands.description: Drawing and labelling simple pictures.

contentStandards.description: Draw and label simple pictures

indicators.description: Draw and label objects found in their environment

exemplars.description: Take learners round to look at charts showing labelled objects.
Put learners into groups and ask them to choose an area in the environment where they will want to make a list of objects found there (e.g. home, market, shops etc.).
Let learners draw and label objects from the area studied by their group.
Help them to edit their work particularly spelling and spacing.
Let learners write their names under their work and post their charts on the walls of the classroom for peer review.

subStrands.title: Writing Simple Words and Sentences
subStrands.description: Using grammar and vocabulary to write correctly.

contentStandards.description: Use knowledge of grammar and vocabulary to write words and sentences correctly.

indicators.description: Write simple sentences to express feelings

exemplars.description: Put learners in groups to share their feelings.
Let each one write, at least, one sentence to express a feeling, e.g. "I am happy."

indicators.description: Write simple and meaningful sentences on objects found in the environment

exemplars.description: Take learners out on a field-trip outside the school to observe things.

Discuss the trip and write their observations in simple sentences on the board. e.g. i. There is a blue house near the school. ii. The house is small. iii. I saw a big bus. iv. The bus has a driver. v. A big shop is near the school. vi. Taxi cabs are on the road. etc.
Put learners into groups to write simple sentences about the objects and places found in the environment.
Encourage each group to add pictures to their sentences.
Publish their work on the walls and encourage gallery walk.

indicators.description: Draw a picture and write at least a sentence to share an opinion

exemplars.description: Show pictures of 'smiley/images on your phone or card', e.g. smiling, angry, indifferent or frightened faces, etc.
Let learners study the pictures and interpret them.
Let learners, in pairs, discuss their opinions. Note: The learner's opinion is very important and whatever interpretation learners give must be accepted.

subStrands.title: Controlled Writing
subStrands.description: Writing simple compositions.

contentStandards.description: Write simple compositions

indicators.description: Write or copy correct sentences from substitution tables

exemplars.description: Have a simple 3-4 column substitution table on the board. e.g. [I/We/The Boys] [go to/play at/read in] [School/Home/the park].
Have learners identify the words that make up the table.
With an example, let learners form sentences from the substitution table.
Have learners read out their sentences and write down their sentences in their books.

indicators.description: Match parts of sentences to compose meaningful texts

exemplars.description: Let learners talk about the topic (My House) by using descriptive words in sentences.
Write the sentences on the board. e.g. i. My house is big. ii. The walls are blue. iii. The house has many windows. iv. The windows are big. v. The doors and windows are blue.
Write the sentences and break each into two parts for learners to match the beginning with their correct endings.
Encourage learners to do peer editing.

contentStandards.description: Matching parts of sentences to composition

indicators.description: Re-arrange jumbled sentences logically

exemplars.description: Tell/Read an interesting story to learners.
Let them retell the story.
Jumble up the sentences making up the story and ask learners to re-arrange them.

subStrands.title: Guided Composition
subStrands.description: Composing short paragraphs.

contentStandards.description: Compose short paragraphs through answering questions

indicators.description: Develop two coherent paragraphs on one idea or concepts using leading questions

exemplars.description: Write selected topics on the board, e.g. "Myself".
Teacher and learners brainstorm to generate ideas about the topic.
Put learners in groups and ask leading questions to guide them develop the ideas generated into one or two paragraphs.

subStrands.title: Narrative Writing
subStrands.description: Narrating situations and expressing feelings.

contentStandards.description: Narrate situations, express feelings and convey point of view about the real or fictional world

indicators.description: Write about real or imagined experiences or events using the process approach

exemplars.description: Ask learners simple questions on their daily routines.
Let learners brainstorm and choose a topic for the day. e. g. "A visit to the market" or "A visit to the beach"
Using questions, assist learners to write a paragraph or two about their experiences. e. g. i. What is the name of the market? ii. Where is the market? iii. What did you buy from the market?
Let learners write a short paragraph and paste it on the notice board. Note: Learners may create imaginary experiences and write about them.

subStrands.title: Descriptive Writing
subStrands.description: Demonstrating knowledge of description in writing.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of description in writing

indicators.description: Use simple sentences to describe feelings

exemplars.description: Let learners name and describe common objects using adjectives.
Let learners name various objects in the classroom.
Explain what they have to do.
Demonstrate the activity by describing an object in 3-5 sentences. Write the sentences on the board.
Let individuals choose objects and describe them orally and then in writing.
